(This was my text transcript before my video review at the bottom of the post).
+++Intro+++

Hi I'm R0ot2U with today's game review.

+++Game+++

The game is STASIS created by indie developer THE BROTHERHOOD, it's an isometric 2D Adventure game with a very defined brand of Horror / Jump Scare and sci-fi fantasy feel. This game does not aim to hold the players hands through it's roughly 8 hours of game-play and has at times a very dark sense of humour.

+++Summary / Setup+++
Your intro scene sets up your home for the duration of the game as the Groomlake in a decaying orbit around Neptune, a massive mining ship which has been refitted for "other" purposes. This scene gives me a real Event Horizon feel and some of the game resonates the same feeling later on.

You play John Maracheck who having just been abruptly dropped from a STASIS tank and is suffering serious physical complications and your first task is to find medical attention. The Groomlake seems deserted with John already voicing that it's not his ship and your only companion is the ships robotic system informing you of your critical condition. Soon you realize you were not alone and have lost the two most precious people in the universe to you - your wife and daughter. A flashback brings you to the pre-STASIS scene and to one of the most ironic and creepy lullabies I've ever heard.

The entire game's design keeps you spooked, paranoid and terrified as to what is going to happen with your next step or interaction with absolutely anything around you. The music ranges from gentle lullabies hiding what is only impending doom to heart attack inducing crescendos bringing you back to childhood memories of hiding under your blanket in the dark for safety, although this time the blanket won't be enough to save you.

++++What do you do?+++

Like most point and click adventure games your tasks will involve reading through the, novel length, PDA and computer entries from the crew, noticing subtle clues scrawled in blood, bolted to doors or stuck to screens and using those clues to solve the various tasks and puzzles that block your path to locating your wife and child.

+++How did you find the game? Play-style, re-playability, graphics, story, mood, sounds etc+++

This game ticks all the boxes for me, it's terrifying, difficult in places enough to make you keep playing and not relegate the game files to your recycle bin. It challenges your mental capacity and state constantly and has one of the better storylines I've come across in any game in quite awhile. You have your suspected villain and your friend and they give you attachment to the game that I genuinely felt satisfied at the finish.

For most you might not get more than one play-through of this game but I'd highly recommend going back and reading the various journal entries across all the levels.

The artwork in this game suits it perfectly, it's completed to a high standard and maintains the gritty, gore filled world of the Groomlake. The mood like the story is one of constant horror and hope combined although you lose more hope as it progresses. The music as already mentioned is by far my favourite part of the game and I'd advise purchasing the slightly more expensive version of the game as you get the soundtrack along with it.

If you've got a weak stomach or have no love for gore and human experimentation and torture then you may want to go play hello kitty adventure but if you want a truly horrifying experience that isn't your horror at terrible game-play then pick up a copy of STASIS.

+++Where can you get the game?+++
The game is available through Steam and GOG.com and retails for 24.99 Euro before any sales adjustment.

+++Outro+++

As always you've been you and I'm R0ot2U saying "see you on the next review". If you liked the video please like and subscribe to the channel for more upcoming content.

I agree with the main point that many of the studies are essentially putting the horse before the carriage. At the same time though, I think they're a bit too quick to jump to conclusions about the mental effects of obesity. I think it's a pretty extreme claim to say that if you took a fit person, changed their eating habits to a calorie heavy diet and removed exercise, that there wouldn't be a big drop in functionality in almost every area. I think anyone who's suffered from an injury and had to take time to recuperate can attest to how depressing it is to suddenly be removed from the world like that. And obesity has a pretty similar effect in forcing limitations to activity and even social interaction. It seems fairly obvious that long term this would turn into decreased performance in most mental tasks. Obesity would cause depression, depression would cause lowered motivation and attention, that would turn into lowered performance.

It's been known for decades that low self-control relates to poorer performance outcomes in school (longitudinal studies + marshmallow test with kids). I bet fat people with skinny/normal parents are especially low on the intelligence/academic performance scale because their fatness was more facilitated by low impulse control and low self control, rather than because of feeder/negligent parents.
